messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I haven’t agreed to it; don’t treat my silence or family ties as consent. B should be heard about what she needs, but I can’t decide for her. I want clear information, room for each of us to speak, and no pressure or decisions presented as settled. Your wording fits; I’d add that disagreement shouldn’t be treated as obstruction. No major discomfort, though that’s a lot of questions at once.

I’d like to buy it with my husband at a family discount; building financial security matters to me. C hasn’t agreed, so nothing can move ahead yet. Your wording fits. The questions are a little much all at once, but I’m okay answering. Prices, shares, and timing aren’t settled.

Thank you. I’d like some money to start a dance studio, so what happens with the house and will matters to me partly because of what I may receive. I know A wants to buy the house and C hasn’t agreed; I don’t know what price, shares, or timing would be fair, and I wouldn’t want those treated as settled yet. I’d like my sisters to understand that the studio matters to me. Your wording mostly fits. I’m a little uncomfortable being asked about so many things at once, but it’s all right.
All fit. I don’t have anything else to add right now. It’s still a lot in one message, but manageable.
#1 is how I pursue what matters most: well-being. The rest fits. And the questions are still a little much at once.
Yes, that wording fits. I don’t have anything else to add right now.
Only #1: I’d say, “I want money to help me start the dance studio.” The other two fit. I don’t have anything else to add right now.
Not exactly—I want money to help me start the studio, but I’m not sure that wording captures an underlying need. I don’t have anything else to add, and this pace is okay.
It would give me a little more freedom to make my own choices. I don’t think I’ve held anything else back, and I’m okay with this pace.
Yes, that fits. No minor discomfort.
I can’t say they all fit yet; it’s a lot to take in at once. Please keep my interest in buying with my husband at a family discount visible as a possibility, not an agreed outcome.
All fit for now. I don’t have a minor discomfort to add.

I’m uncomfortable with drafts that make every possible sale or paper require all three yeses. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase; I haven’t set a rule for every other option. And I can’t confirm A’s or B’s needs for them. Slow down.

That fits. I want to consider each proposal on its own, with clear information, so I’m not pre-committing to options I haven’t seen or letting my refusal of A’s discount be treated as agreement to something else. No discomfort with pausing.
